item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The log is incredibly unclear as to who, exactly, was at that birthday party. It mentions "staff", but it's ambiguous as to whether that was staff at the birthday party venue, or if it was a Foundation staff birthday party - which would explain the accelerated timeline.

In general, the "anecdotal" experiment log style doesn't do this SCP any favors. "Hey, the situation is weird, so let me tell it in story form rather than as an incident log." The whole point of standardized logs is that they make events and individuals as unambiguous as possible to prevent confusion, and the anecdotal style makes it incredibly ambiguous and

The article as a whole is just so unnecessarily prosaic, and it doesn't explore basic elements of the SCP. The only description of a candy's effect we have are for the super-duper candy, and even that is explicitly an exception case. What happens when someone eats a "regular" grade candy? Do they visibly regress in age instantly? Do they get the years back at the same rate as the song drained them? What happens if someone eats someone else's candy?

I get that it's an old article, but even by the standards of Series I it's half-baked.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Let's take a look at the timeline for that party.
Assume the high-end of 4 seconds per verse.

At t=0, the present is unwrapped and monkey starts to sing.
After ten verses, 40 seconds, Recipient starts trying to turn it off.
After possibly ten more, 80 seconds, Recipient is visibly aged.
5 more verses, 100 seconds, Recipient is physically exhausted and begs for help.
Then possibly as many as 40 more verses, 260 seconds from unwrapping, a containment team shows up to find a skeleton.

We are told the party goers had slothful reaction, so they didn't call 911 right at the 100 second mark. Meaning they got in touch with emergency services, Foundation surveillance recognized a new anomaly was being discussed, intercepted the dispatch, and a recovery team arrived on site all in something less than three minutes.

That would be a decent response time if this party was happening in the break room of Site 19; and rather unbelievable for the random civilian office the story implies.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
If you don't already know, this SCP has become semi-famous thanks to its addition in the latest version of the SCP Containment Breach Unity remake (see Youtube for footage). It's suitably creepy in that with a nightmarish monkey design although the specifics are a bit different to the actual article.

I came across this SCP by chance reading through Neko's articles. It's a cool little idea with a catchy/disturbing song to go with it. The pills though are a layer the game doesn't really examine and were definitely cool and unexpected.

There are a few things that don't quite hold up though that might warrant fixing, especially considering this SCP will probably be getting a lot of traffic right now.

As someone else mentioned, when the personnel is singing along, it doesn't say whether she is actually visibly ageing or not. If she is ageing and it takes 45 repetitions to succeed at the song, then how can middle-aged/older people survive the curse (they'd probably die of old age before they can "win")? Or does the monkey stop singing when you exactly match the pitch of the song, for example. I think we just need a little more detail as by that attempt they should know a bit more.

The other thing that really stood out was the initial finding of the SCP. I like the setup of the office party, it's a chilling little scene. However it's very unbelieveable that a containment team could get there so fast. In the article it says each verse is one line and has a gap of 4/5 seconds between verses. After 40 verses or something a containment team arrives on scene. So somehow a Foundation team gets to this random party in just a couple of minutes, in time to see the end of the song? How? And how would they even know? I'd just have them arrive later on once its reported.

item.title: Possible picture for SCP-983
item.content:encoded:
I love this little guy, and I have a couple of questions regarding it.

1) The sing-a-long requirements mention matching the timing of SCP-983's jolly little ditty, but they don't mention having to match the pitch of its singing. Does the accuracy of a test subjects pitch have an effect upon the quality of candy they receive? I'd love to think so, as 'Happy Birthday' sing-a-longs are notorious for everyone who is singing in the group to vary wildly in pitch, tone, and phrasing, producing a 'chaotic chorus' effect.

2) Has a picture ever been considered for SCP-983? Would the original author / admins object to one being added to the article? I dug up what I thought were 3 appropriate photos and posted them on my sandbox page, and I encourage people to have a look-a-long and comment here upon their suitability.

item.content:encoded:
I have got a few issues with this article.

One, the description of properties of such candy when they are first mentioned seems to me to be inconsistent with results of testing. Unless transforming someone into an energy-based life form counts as giving them extra energy… in which case it doesn't match the clinical tone expected of SCP files.

Two, the test log doesn't say anything about the subject regaining lost age before going nova. Given the subject was kept for observation for an hour after consuming the candy, I would expect this effect to occur some time during that time period.

And finally, does any candy produced by the monkey only affect the singer when consumed, or would the same happen to someone else? Or perhaps anyone can eat the candy but it's still the singer who gets affected? Specifically, I wonder what would happen if someone else ate a piece of age-restoring candy.

All the above aside, this is an interesting and quite well-executed SCP. Upvoted!
